records.section_heading: New records and notes on marine benthic algae of American Samoa-Chlorophyta & Phaeophyta<sup>1</sup>
records.question: How many species were added to the previously known flora of the benthic marine algae of American Samoa, and how many of these additions were Chlorophyta and Phaeophyta?
records.ground_truth_answer: A total of 43 species were added; of these, 35 were Chlorophyta and 8 were Phaeophyta, raising the known flora to 230 species.
ground_truth_chunks: **Abstract** — A total of 43 species are added to the previously known flora of the benthic marine algae of American Samoa (8 Phaeophyta, 35 Chlorophyta), raising the known flora to 230 species.

records.question: How many algal species did William Albert Setchell compile for American Samoa in 1924, and how were they distributed among major algal groups?
records.ground_truth_answer: Setchell compiled 100 species: 13 Cyanophyta, 47 Rhodophyta, 11 Phaeophyta, and 29 Chlorophyta.
ground_truth_chunks: Setchell compiled 100 species, including 13 Cyanophyta, 47 Rhodophyta, 11 Phaeophyta and 29 Chlorophyta, from about 15 sites, primarily on Tutuila and Aunu'u islands.

records.question: How can Dictyopteris repens be differentiated from Dictyopteris delicatula?
records.ground_truth_answer: Dictyopteris repens lacks the submarginal rib seen in D. delicatula: D. delicatula has a submarginal rib, whereas the margins of D. repens remain distromatic. Additionally, D. delicatula's distribution appears to halt in Fiji with no reports from Samoa.
ground_truth_chunks: The two can be differentiated by a submarginal rib in *D. delicatula* whereas the margins of *D. repens* remain distromatic.
Furthermore, the distribution of *D. delicatula* appears to halt in Fiji with no reports of its presence in Samoa.

records.question: Why could the Dictyota specimen not be fully determined to species?
records.ground_truth_answer: Because only infertile material was collected; determination would be possible after collecting reproductive specimens.
ground_truth_chunks: Only infertile material was collected and appears to be quite distinct from the other epiphytic *Dictyota* species (*D. friabilis*). Determination would be possible following the collection of reproductive specimens.

records.question: Which species was collected epiphytic on the base of Sargassum anapense at Amalau?
ground_truth_chunks: Sporocladopsis erythraea Nasr 1944: 33 (type locality: Red Sea). (Figs 6-8)
This rarity was collected only from Amalau, epiphytic on the base of Sargassum anapense Setchell.

records.question: Where was the single specimen of Codium cf. mamillosum collected?
records.ground_truth_answer: Utulei Point, near the mouth of Pago Pago Harbour, Tutuila Island.
ground_truth_chunks: A single specimen was collected from Utulei Point, near the mouth of Pago Pago Harbour.
Voucher specimens: Tutuila Island: Utulei, S. Cole, P. Reath, V. Bonito, P. Skelton & L. Basch 13.x.2002 (AS 178)

records.question: Which morphological stage of Derbesia marina was found at American Samoa?
ground_truth_chunks: Two very contrasting morphological stages are reported, the spherical *Halicystis* or the gametophytic stage and the filamentous *Derbesia* sporophytic stage.
The latter stage was the only stage found at American Samoa.
The cylindrical filaments (40-62.5 µm diam.) are irregularly and sparsely branched, with a double septum at the base of some branches, and are found entangled with other algae.

records.question: Which Halimeda species is described as common in the upper subtidal (ca 5 m depth) with segments reminiscent of Halimeda opuntia but larger and less profusely branching?
records.ground_truth_answer: Halimeda gracilis Harvey ex J. Agardh 1887.
ground_truth_chunks: Halimeda gracilis Harvey ex J. Agardh 1887: 82 (type locality: Sri Lanka). Common in the upper subtidal (ca 5 m depth) in moderate water flow. The segments are reminiscent of Halimeda opuntia (Linnaeus) Lamouroux but are larger and less profusely branching in more than one plane.

Voucher specimens: Tutuila Island: Vatia Bay, S. Cole, P. Reath, V. Bonito, P. Skelton & L. Basch 16.x.2002 (AS 20); Leloaloa, S. Cole, P. Reath, V. Bonito, P. Skelton & L. Basch 17.x.2002 (AS 85); Aoa Bay, P.A. Skelton 12.ix.2003 (AS 354);

records.question: Which Parvocaulis species is described as having its rays arranged in a single plane?
ground_truth_chunks: Parvocaulis clavata is similar to P. exigua (Solms-Laubach) Berger et al. (2003) but can be separated by the rounded ray tips (versus mamillate tips in P. exigua). Moreover, the rays are arranged in a single plane (Abbott & Huisman 2004).
Abbott & Huisman (2004) observed the rays to be arranged in more than one plane, as opposed to the single plane in P. clavata.

records.question: How many marine benthic algal species are reported from American Samoa in the latest compilation, and how are they distributed among Rhodophyta, Phaeophyta, and Chlorophyta?
records.ground_truth_answer: The latest compilation reports 230 marine benthic algal species from American Samoa: 133 Rhodophyta, 23 Phaeophyta, and 74 Chlorophyta.
ground_truth_chunks: With the additions reported here, the latest compilation of marine benthic algal species reported from American Samoa is 230, comprising 133 Rhodophyta, 23 Phaeophyta and 74 Chlorophyta.
